# Requirements — `2026-07-28`

Every normative clause of the `2026-07-28` specification that the validator's registry carries — 501 in all, 181 judged from a recorded trace and 320 excluded with the reason below. A report names a clause by the ID used as each heading here; each entry quotes the specification verbatim and links to the published text. `mcp-trace-validator requirements --revision 2026-07-28 --format json` prints the same data as JSON.

## BASE

### BASE-041

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> Cross-cutting concerns like logging and argument completion All implementations MUST support the base protocol, versioning, and the message patterns.

[`basic/index`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic)

**Excluded.** The umbrella clause the BASE area mechanizes requirement-by-requirement; it has no observable beyond its constituents. Same role as BASE-012 at 2025-11-25, widened by this revision from 'base protocol and lifecycle management' to 'base protocol, versioning, and the message patterns'.

### BASE-042

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> All messages between MCP clients and servers MUST follow the JSON-RPC 2.0 specification.

[`basic/index#messages`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#messages)

Judged by `base.jsonrpc-version`.

### BASE-043

**MUST** · binds the client and server

[`basic/index#requests`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#requests)

Judged by `base.request-id-type`.

### BASE-044

**MUST NOT** · binds the client and server

> Unlike base JSON-RPC, the ID MUST NOT be `null`.

[`basic/index#requests`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#requests)

Judged by `base.request-id-not-null`.

### BASE-045

**MUST NOT** · binds the client and server

> The request ID MUST NOT match the ID of any other request the sender has issued and not yet received a response for.

[`basic/index#requests`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#requests)

Judged by `base.request-id-unique-in-flight`.

### BASE-046

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> Result responses MUST include the same ID as the request they correspond to.

[`basic/index#result-responses`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#result-responses)

Judged by `base.result-id-matches`.

### BASE-047

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> Result responses MUST include a `result` field.

[`basic/index#result-responses`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#result-responses)

Judged by `base.result-field`.

### BASE-048

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> The `result` MUST include a `resultType` field to indicate the type of the result.

[`basic/index#result-responses`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#result-responses)

Judged by `base.result-type-present`.

### BASE-049

**MUST** · binds the client

> The set of supported `ResultType` values MUST be created from the set defined in the core protocol and include any additional values of supported extensions that are advertised via capabilities.

[`basic/index#result-responses`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#result-responses)

**Excluded.** The client's set of supported `ResultType` values is internal state assembled from the core protocol plus its advertised extensions; a trace shows the values a server sent, never the set the client was willing to accept.

### BASE-050

**MUST** · binds the client

> A `resultType` of any value unrecognized by the client MUST be considered invalid.

[`basic/index#result-responses`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#result-responses)

**Excluded.** What a client 'considers invalid' is internal judgment. The observable consequence — a client refusing to proceed — is client conduct after receipt, outside a server-side trace, and indistinguishable from any other reason it stopped.

### BASE-051

**MUST** · binds the client

> For backward compatibility with servers implementing earlier protocol versions, which do not include `resultType`, clients MUST treat an absent `resultType` as `"complete"`.

[`basic/index#result-responses`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#result-responses)

**Excluded.** The backward-compatibility rule binds the client's *interpretation* of an absent field, which leaves no wire artifact: the trace records that `resultType` was absent, not that the client read it as `complete`.

### BASE-052

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> Error responses MUST include the same ID as the request they correspond to (except in error cases where the ID could not be read due a malformed request).

[`basic/index#error-responses`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#error-responses)

Judged by `base.error-id-matches`.

### BASE-053

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> Error responses MUST include an `error` field with a `code` and `message`.

[`basic/index#error-responses`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#error-responses)

Judged by `base.error-shape`.

### BASE-054

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> Error codes MUST be integers.

[`basic/index#error-responses`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#error-responses)

Judged by `base.error-code-integer`.

### BASE-055

**MUST NOT** · binds the client and server

> New codes MUST NOT be allocated in this sub-range

[`basic/index#error-codes`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#error-codes)

**Excluded.** Binds allocation — assigning a new meaning to a code in -32000..-32019 — which is an act of whoever defines codes, not a message. A code observed on the wire carries no record of when or by whom it was allocated, so a legacy code in use is indistinguishable from a newly allocated one. Its use is the sentence's other half, BASE-083, which is a SHOULD NOT and is checked at that level: until 2026-10-04 this entry carried both halves at MUST NOT and reported every use of -32000 as a MUST failure.

### BASE-083

**SHOULD NOT** · binds the client and server

> new implementations SHOULD NOT use codes from this sub-range at all.

[`basic/index#error-codes`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#error-codes)

Judged by `base.error-code-legacy-subrange`.

### BASE-056

**MUST NOT** · binds the client and server

> Apart from `-32002` (see below), receivers MUST NOT assume any specific meaning for these codes.

[`basic/index#error-codes`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#error-codes)

**Excluded.** What a receiver assumes about a legacy code's meaning is internal; only conduct following from the assumption could surface, and attributing it requires the assumption. Same boundary as BASE-025 for reserved `_meta` keys.

### BASE-057

**MUST NOT** · binds the client and server

> Implementations MUST NOT emit any code from this sub-range that is not defined by this specification and MUST use defined codes only with their specified meanings.

[`basic/index#error-codes`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#error-codes)

Judged by `base.error-code-reserved-subrange`.

### BASE-058

**MUST NOT** · binds the client and server

> Implementations of this protocol version MUST NOT emit these codes:

[`basic/index#error-codes`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#error-codes)

Judged by `base.error-code-withdrawn`.

### BASE-059

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> Clients SHOULD still accept `-32002` from servers implementing earlier versions.

[`basic/index#error-codes`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#error-codes)

**Excluded.** Client-side acceptance of a legacy code is internal handling; the trace records the `-32002` a server sent, not whether the client honoured it. The emitting side is judged by BASE-058.

### BASE-060

**SHOULD** · binds the client and server

> New error codes for purposes not defined by this specification SHOULD be allocated outside the JSON-RPC reserved range (`-32768` to `-32000`); the remainder of the integer space is available for application-defined errors.

[`basic/index#error-codes`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#error-codes)

Judged by `base.error-code-application-range`.

### BASE-061

**MUST NOT** · binds the client and server

> The receiver MUST NOT send a response.

[`basic/index#notifications`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#notifications)

**Excluded.** A response to a notification carries no correlating ID, so it is indistinguishable on the wire from any other unsolicited response; unsolicited responses are flagged by `base.result-id-matches` and `base.error-id-matches`. Same reasoning as BASE-011 at 2025-11-25.

### BASE-062

**MUST NOT** · binds the client and server

> Notifications MUST NOT include an ID.

[`basic/index#notifications`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#notifications)

Judged by `base.notification-no-id`.

### BASE-063

**MUST NOT** · binds the server

> Servers MUST NOT rely on prior requests over the same connection to establish context (e.g., capabilities, protocol version, client identity).

[`basic/index#statelessness`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#statelessness)

**Excluded.** Reliance is internal reasoning. A server that answers correctly may or may not have consulted prior requests, and one that errors may have done so for any reason; the trace shows the answer, not the inference behind it. The adjacent observable is that every request carries its own context, judged by BASE-030.

### BASE-064

**SHOULD** · binds the server

> Servers SHOULD be prepared to handle requests associated with multiple tasks, threads, or conversations.

[`basic/index#statelessness`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#statelessness)

**Excluded.** Preparedness is a property of the server's implementation, not of any session it took part in; a trace that happens to interleave conversations evidences capability, while one that does not evidences nothing.

### BASE-065

**SHOULD NOT** · binds the server

> Servers SHOULD NOT require that a client reuse the same connection or process to perform related operations.

[`basic/index#statelessness`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#statelessness)

**Excluded.** Falsifying this needs a server refusing an operation *because* it arrived on a different connection — two correlated connections in one recording, which the trace vocabulary does not span: each recorded session is one transport.

### BASE-066

**SHOULD NOT** · binds the client

> Clients SHOULD NOT use an individual task, thread, or conversation as the lifetime boundary for the stdio process.

[`basic/index#statelessness`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#statelessness)

**Excluded.** Process lifetime is host-OS conduct outside the trace event vocabulary — `transport-open`/`close`/`abort` record that a transport ended, not what the client tied its lifetime to. Same boundary as LIFE-014 at 2025-11-25.

### BASE-067

**MUST** · binds the client

> State that needs to span multiple requests (e.g., long-running tasks, application-level handles) MUST be referenced by an explicit identifier the client passes on each request.

[`basic/index#statelessness`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#statelessness)

**Excluded.** Which state 'needs to span multiple requests' is server-internal; the trace shows the arguments a client passed, not whether they carried everything the server required. A violation surfaces only as the server failing for some other stated reason.

### BASE-068

**SHOULD NOT** · binds the client and server

> Implementations using an HTTP-based transport SHOULD conform to this specification, whereas implementations using STDIO transport SHOULD NOT follow this specification, and instead retrieve credentials from the environment.

[`basic/index#auth`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#auth)

**Excluded.** Credential retrieval from the environment is process-local conduct with no wire footprint, and the HTTP half defers to the authorization specification, whose clauses are entered on its own pages: AUTH-086 and AUTH-087 restate this sentence there, and the challenge clauses a recording can judge carry checks. Same decision as BASE-085 at 2025-11-25.

**Excluded.** Dialect support is validation behavior inside each implementation; a trace shows schemas exchanged, not which dialects the receiver could handle. Same reasoning as BASE-013 at 2025-11-25.

**MUST** · binds the client and server

**Excluded.** Graceful handling is receiver conduct; the trace would show an error, but not that it was raised for an unsupported dialect rather than any other malformed-schema reason. Same reasoning as BASE-015 at 2025-11-25.

### BASE-072

[`basic/index#implementation-requirements`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#implementation-requirements)

### BASE-074

**MUST NOT** · binds the client and server

[`basic/index#$ref-resolution`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#$ref-resolution)

### BASE-075

**MUST** · binds the client and server

**SHOULD** · binds the client and server

## TRAN

### TRAN-050

**MUST** · binds the server

> The server MUST provide a single HTTP endpoint path (hereafter referred to as the MCP endpoint) that supports POST.

[`basic/transports/streamable-http`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http)

**Excluded.** Endpoint topology — how many paths a server exposes and which methods each accepts — is deployment configuration; a recorded session shows one endpoint being used, never the set that exists. Same reasoning as TRAN-006 at 2025-11-25.

### TRAN-051

**MUST** · binds the server

> Servers MUST validate the `Origin` header on all incoming connections to prevent DNS rebinding attacks.

[`basic/transports/streamable-http#security-&-endpoint`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http#security-&-endpoint)

**Excluded.** Origin validation is server-internal policy applied before any MCP message; the trace records admitted sessions, not the requests a policy refused. Same reasoning as TRAN-002 at 2025-11-25; the everything server's policy middleware is tested directly in http_policy.rs.

### TRAN-052

**MUST** · binds the server

> If the `Origin` header is present and invalid, servers MUST respond with HTTP 403 Forbidden.

[`basic/transports/streamable-http#security-&-endpoint`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http#security-&-endpoint)

**Excluded.** A refused request never becomes an MCP session, so the 403 it drew is outside what the tap records. Same reasoning as TRAN-007 at 2025-11-25; enforced in code and covered by the server's own policy tests.

### TRAN-053

**SHOULD** · binds the server

> When running locally, servers SHOULD bind only to localhost (127.0.0.1) rather than all network interfaces (0.0.0.0).

[`basic/transports/streamable-http#security-&-endpoint`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http#security-&-endpoint)

**Excluded.** Bind address is process configuration with no wire footprint. Same reasoning as TRAN-008 at 2025-11-25.

### TRAN-054

**SHOULD** · binds the server

> Servers SHOULD implement proper authentication for all connections.

[`basic/transports/streamable-http#security-&-endpoint`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http#security-&-endpoint)

**Excluded.** Whether authentication is properly implemented is not decidable from one session's headers: the client's credential is never recorded, and the server's validation of it is internal. What a recording does show — the challenge a protected server answers with — is judged under the authorization pages' own clauses (AUTH-097, AUTH-124, AUTH-129–AUTH-133). Same reasoning as TRAN-009 at 2025-11-25.

### TRAN-055

**MUST** · binds the client

> Every JSON-RPC message sent from the client MUST be a new HTTP POST request to the MCP endpoint.

[`basic/transports/streamable-http#sending-messages`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http#sending-messages)

**Excluded.** Adds to TRAN-056's verb obligation that each message ride a *new* POST to the MCP endpoint. A POST body is one JSON value, which a recorder writes as one payload, so more than one message in a POST is a non-object body — TRAN-059 judges that. What remains — that the request was new rather than reused, and was addressed to the MCP endpoint — leaves no trace: the endpoint is not recorded. Same split as TRAN-024/TRAN-049 at 2025-11-25.

### TRAN-056

**MUST** · binds the client

### TRAN-063

**MUST NOT** · binds the server

### DISC-001

**MUST** · binds the server

[`server/discover`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/discover)

Judged by `discover.implemented`.

### DISC-002

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> A client that supports both modern (per-request `meta`) and legacy (`initialize` handshake) servers SHOULD send `server/discover` first; see stdio: Backward Compatibility for the fallback rules.

[`server/discover#when-to-call`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/discover#when-to-call)

Judged by `discover.dual-era-probe-first`.

### DISC-003

**SHOULD** · binds the server

> `meta['io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo']`: Name and version of the server software. Servers SHOULD include this field.

[`server/discover#discoverresult`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/discover#discoverresult)

Judged by `discover.server-info-included`.

### DISC-004

**SHOULD NOT** · binds the client

> `serverInfo` is self-reported by the server and is not verified by the protocol. It is intended for display, logging, and debugging. Clients SHOULD NOT use it to change their behavior, and SHOULD NOT rely on it for security decisions.

[`server/discover#discoverresult`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/discover#discoverresult)

**Excluded.** Binds what the client does with `serverInfo` after reading it — behaviour changes and security decisions are internal reasoning, and a trace records the messages, not the inferences drawn from them. Same boundary as BASE-022's icon-consumer clauses.

## VERS

### VERS-001

**MUST** · binds the server

> If the server does not implement the requested version (whether the version is unknown to the server, or is a known version the server has chosen not to support), it MUST respond with an `UnsupportedProtocolVersionError` listing the versions it does support:

[`basic/versioning#protocol-version-negotiation`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning#protocol-version-negotiation)

Judged by `transport.unsupported-version-error`.

### VERS-002

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> The client SHOULD select a mutually supported version from the `supported` list and retry the request, or surface an error to the user if no compatible version exists.

[`basic/versioning#protocol-version-negotiation`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning#protocol-version-negotiation)

Judged by `versioning.retry-uses-supported-version`.

### VERS-003

**MUST** · binds the server

> Servers MUST implement `server/discover`.

[`basic/versioning#protocol-version-negotiation`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning#protocol-version-negotiation)

Judged by `discover.implemented`.

### VERS-004

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> Extension identifiers MUST follow the `meta` key naming rules, with a mandatory prefix.

[`basic/versioning#extension-negotiation`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning#extension-negotiation)

Judged by `versioning.extension-identifier-format`.

### VERS-005

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> If one party supports an extension but the other does not, the supporting party MUST either revert to core protocol behavior or reject the request with an appropriate error.

[`basic/versioning#extension-negotiation`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning#extension-negotiation)

**Excluded.** Both permitted responses are defined by the extension, not by this specification: what "core protocol behavior" looks like for a given extension, and which error is "appropriate", are each stated in that extension's own document. Where an official extension's clauses are entered (tasks and skills, beside this revision), they judge exactly that, in the extension's own block and never scored (ADR-0023): TASK-001, for one, is this clause for the tasks extension. Judging it here, among the core's clauses, would let an optional extension's behaviour move the core verdict.

### VERS-006

**SHOULD** · binds the client and server

> Extensions SHOULD document their expected fallback behavior.

[`basic/versioning#extension-negotiation`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning#extension-negotiation)

**Excluded.** Binds an extension's documentation, not either party's messages. The subject is not even a session participant: no recorded trace can be evidence about whether a document exists.

### VERS-007

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> Clients SHOULD cache the result for the lifetime of the server process (stdio) or origin (HTTP), and MAY persist it across restarts of the same server configuration, re-probing if the cached assumption later fails.

[`basic/versioning#backward-compatibility-with-initialization-based-versions`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning#backward-compatibility-with-initialization-based-versions)

**Excluded.** The cached value is the era determination — client-internal state, and the clause's horizon is the server process or origin, which outlives the recorded session. The one wire-visible candidate, a repeated probe, is not evidence: the clause's own "re-probing if the cached assumption later fails" permits it.

### VERS-008

**SHOULD** · binds the server

> A server that supports only modern versions SHOULD name the protocol versions it supports in any error it returns to an `initialize` request, on any transport: legacy clients have no fall-forward mechanism, and this message may be the only diagnostic they can surface to users.

[`basic/versioning#backward-compatibility-with-initialization-based-versions`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning#backward-compatibility-with-initialization-based-versions)

Judged by `versioning.initialize-error-names-versions`.

### VERS-009

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> Modern | Legacy | Fails. The server may reject the request with an implementation-defined error, stay silent, or even process an era-ambiguous method under legacy semantics. On stdio, clients SHOULD send `server/discover` first to fail deterministically; the client then surfaces an actionable error to the user.

[`basic/versioning#compatibility-matrix`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning#compatibility-matrix)

**Excluded.** The compatibility matrix's modern-client, legacy-server row. Its antecedent is the server being legacy, which is exactly what an unprobed exchange fails to reveal — the row itself says such a server may reject the request, stay silent, or process it under legacy semantics — and, as for TRAN-142, a recording cannot show that its first request was the client's first. The dual-era form of the same advice is TRAN-128, judged where a session witnesses both eras.

## TRAN

### TRAN-110

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> JSON-RPC messages MUST be UTF-8 encoded.

[`basic/transports/index#messages`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports#messages)

**Excluded.** Restates TRAN-001 at 2025-11-25, whose exclusion this project already argued and which holds unchanged: trace documents are UTF-8 by construction, so recorded messages prove nothing was mis-encoded, and absence is not evidence because capture tooling drops undecodable bytes. Violations surface as capture-time parse failures, not trace findings.

### TRAN-111

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> A binding MUST deliver client-sent requests and notifications to the server, and server-sent responses and notifications to the client.

[`basic/transports/index#messages`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports#messages)

**Excluded.** A delivery obligation, and a trace is a record of what arrived: a message the binding failed to deliver is absent from it, and an absent message is indistinguishable from one never sent. The clause's converse — that no other direction exists — is a separate sentence and is enforced where it is stated: TRAN-060 and TRAN-118 for client responses, TRAN-066 and TRAN-120 for server-initiated requests.

### TRAN-112

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> Implementers who choose to support custom transports MUST preserve the JSON-RPC message format, the message patterns, and the per-request metadata model.

[`basic/transports/index#custom-transports`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports#custom-transports)

**Excluded.** No custom transport can appear in a trace: `TransportKind` admits `stdio` and `streamable-http` only, so the clause's subject has no representation in the format this engine reads. What it requires preserved is exactly what the rest of this registry checks for the two standard bindings, against which a custom transport's capture would have to be relabelled first.

### TRAN-113

**SHOULD** · binds the client and server

> Custom transports SHOULD document their connection establishment, message framing, and cancellation patterns to aid interoperability.

[`basic/transports/index#custom-transports`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports#custom-transports)

**Excluded.** Binds a transport's documentation, not its messages. Same class as VERS-006: the artefact the clause requires is a document, and no session can be evidence about whether one exists.

### TRAN-114

**SHOULD** · binds the client and server

> Custom transports that run over a reliable bidirectional byte stream (e.g., Unix domain sockets or TCP) SHOULD reuse the stdio framing rather than defining a new one: the stdio binding is just newline-delimited JSON-RPC over a byte stream, and only its process-lifecycle rules are specific to standard streams.

[`basic/transports/index#custom-transports`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports#custom-transports)

**Excluded.** Binds the design of a transport that cannot be recorded as itself (see TRAN-112), and the property it asks for — which framing was reused — is settled before any message exists. Restated on the stdio page as TRAN-121, with the same reason.

### TRAN-115

**MUST NOT** · binds the client and server

> Messages are delimited by newlines, and MUST NOT contain embedded newlines.

[`basic/transports/stdio`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/stdio)

**Excluded.** Restates TRAN-002 at 2025-11-25 verbatim, and its exclusion holds unchanged: framing is enforced at capture time, the JSON Lines trace format cannot represent an embedded-newline violation, and a parseable trace is evidence the rule held.

### TRAN-116

**SHOULD NOT** · binds the client

> The client MAY capture, forward, or ignore the server's `stderr` output and SHOULD NOT assume `stderr` output indicates error conditions.

[`basic/transports/stdio`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/stdio)

**Excluded.** Binds an inference the client draws from `stderr` — and `stderr` is not part of the recorded message stream at all, so neither the input to that inference nor the inference itself reaches a trace. Same boundary as TRAN-003 at 2025-11-25.

### TRAN-117

**MUST NOT** · binds the server

> The server MUST NOT write anything to its `stdout` that is not a valid MCP message.

[`basic/transports/stdio`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/stdio)

Judged by `transport.stdio-server-output-valid`.

### TRAN-118

**MUST NOT** · binds the client

> The client MUST NOT write anything to the server's `stdin` that is not a valid MCP message.

[`basic/transports/stdio`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/stdio)

Judged by `transport.stdio-client-input-valid`.

### TRAN-119

**MUST NOT** · binds the client

> The client MUST NOT write JSON-RPC responses.

[`basic/transports/stdio#sending-messages`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/stdio#sending-messages)

Judged by `transport.client-no-responses`.

### TRAN-120

**MUST NOT** · binds the server

> The server MUST NOT write JSON-RPC requests to `stdout`.

[`basic/transports/stdio#receiving-messages`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/stdio#receiving-messages)

Judged by `transport.no-independent-server-requests`.

### TRAN-121

**SHOULD** · binds the client and server

> Custom transports built on such streams SHOULD reuse this framing and the message rules on this page; only the subprocess-specific aspects (launch, `stderr`, shutdown by closing the stream, process restart) need channel-specific equivalents.

[`basic/transports/stdio`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/stdio)

**Excluded.** The same clause as TRAN-114, stated from the stdio page's side: a custom transport has no representation in the trace format, and which framing it reused is settled before any message exists.

### TRAN-122

**MUST** · binds the client

> Clients MUST correlate these using the `io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId` field in `meta`; see [`SubscriptionsListenRequest`][subscriptions-listen-request].

[`basic/transports/stdio#receiving-messages`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/stdio#receiving-messages)

**Excluded.** Binds the client's own correlation of notifications it received — bookkeeping inside the client, which produces no message. The wire-visible half of the same mechanism, that the server tags each notification with `io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId`, is BASE-039 and is checked.

### TRAN-123

**MUST** · binds the client

> To cancel an in-flight request, the client MUST send a `notifications/cancelled` notification referencing the request's ID.

[`basic/transports/stdio#cancellation`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/stdio#cancellation)

Judged by `transport.cancel-notification-references-request`.

### TRAN-124

**MUST NOT** · binds the server

> Servers SHOULD stop work on a cancelled request as soon as practical and MUST NOT send any further messages for it.

[`basic/transports/stdio#cancellation`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/stdio#cancellation)

Judged by `transport.no-messages-after-cancel-notification`.

### TRAN-125

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> The client SHOULD initiate shutdown by: Closing the input stream to the child process (the server); Waiting for the server to exit; If the server does not exit within a reasonable time, forcibly terminating the process using the mechanism appropriate for the operating system.

[`basic/transports/stdio#shutdown`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/stdio#shutdown)

**Excluded.** Stream closure, process waits and forced termination are host-OS actions outside the trace event vocabulary — the same reason LIFE-014 excludes the 2025-11-25 shutdown sequence. A `transport-close` lifecycle event records that the transport ended, not which party closed which stream or what it did next.

### TRAN-126

**SHOULD** · binds the server

> Servers SHOULD exit promptly when their standard input is closed or reads return end-of-file.

[`basic/transports/stdio#shutdown`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/stdio#shutdown)

**Excluded.** Both the trigger (stdin closing, or a read returning EOF) and the response (process exit) are host-OS events the trace vocabulary does not carry, and "promptly" is a duration — checks may not consult time, the same limit LIFE-015 records.

### TRAN-127

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> If the server process exits unexpectedly, the client SHOULD restart it.

[`basic/transports/stdio#unexpected-termination`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/stdio#unexpected-termination)

**Excluded.** Process supervision: the antecedent is an unexpected exit and the obligation is to launch a new process, neither of which is a message. A restart also begins a new session, so the evidence would have to span two traces, and nothing in one identifies the other as its successor.

### TRAN-128

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> A client that supports both modern (per-request-metadata) MCP versions and a legacy version that requires an `initialize` handshake SHOULD probe with [`server/discover`][server-discover] before sending any other request, setting its preferred modern version in `meta`.

[`basic/transports/stdio#backward-compatibility`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/stdio#backward-compatibility)

Judged by `discover.dual-era-probe-first`.

### TRAN-129

**MUST NOT** · binds the client

> The fallback MUST NOT be keyed to one specific error code: legacy servers respond to unknown pre-`initialize` requests with implementation-defined errors (commonly `-32601` or `-32602`) or not at all.

[`basic/transports/stdio#backward-compatibility`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/stdio#backward-compatibility)

**Excluded.** Binds the client's decision function, not any message it sends. A session exhibits one probe answered by one error code and one decision taken; whether the client would have fallen back on a *different* code is a property of code paths that session never exercised, and no number of traces settles it.

### TRAN-142

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> A client that only supports modern versions does not need to probe, but probing is still RECOMMENDED: some legacy servers do not validate that a request arrives after `initialize` and would process an era-ambiguous method (such as `tools/call`) under legacy semantics.

[`basic/transports/stdio#backward-compatibility`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/stdio#backward-compatibility)

**Excluded.** Asks a modern-only client to open with a `server/discover` probe, and a recording can show neither half. Not the antecedent: a modern-only client and a dual-era client whose server never forced a fallback send the same messages. Not the order: a modern stdio session has no handshake marking where it began, so a recording that opens on `tools/call` is equally one that started after the probe. The dual-era statement, TRAN-128, is judged by `discover.dual-era-probe-first`, which reports only where a session witnesses both eras; this clause offers no such witness.

## MRTR

### MRTR-001

**MUST** · binds the server

> Servers MUST send server-to-client requests (such as `roots/list`, `sampling/createMessage`, or `elicitation/create`) using the MRTR pattern.

[`basic/patterns/mrtr`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr)

Judged by `transport.no-independent-server-requests`.

### MRTR-002

**MUST** · binds the client

> Every request MUST include the required `meta` fields; see `meta`.

[`basic/patterns/mrtr`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr)

Judged by `meta.required-request-fields`.

### MRTR-003

**MUST NOT** · binds the client

> Clients MUST NOT inspect, parse, modify, or make any assumptions about its contents.

[`basic/patterns/mrtr#inputrequiredresult`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr#inputrequiredresult)

Judged by `mrtr.request-state-echoed`.

### MRTR-004

**MUST NOT** · binds the server

> Servers MUST NOT send `InputRequiredResult` responses on any other client requests.

[`basic/patterns/mrtr#supported-requests`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr#supported-requests)

Judged by `mrtr.input-required-supported-methods`.

### MRTR-005

**MUST** · binds the server

> `inputRequests` keys are server assigned identifiers and MUST be unique within the scope of the request.

[`basic/patterns/mrtr#server-requirements-basic-workflow`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr#server-requirements-basic-workflow)

**Excluded.** JSON object members are unique by the time any check runs: a duplicate key is collapsed by the parser that reads the trace, so a violation cannot survive into the events a check sees. The same reason TRAN-110 and TRAN-115 exclude — the defect is destroyed at parse time, not judged and passed.

### MRTR-006

**MUST** · binds the server

> `inputRequests` values are request objects that MUST be one of `ElicitRequest`, `CreateMessageRequest`, or `ListRootsRequest`

[`basic/patterns/mrtr#server-requirements-basic-workflow`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr#server-requirements-basic-workflow)

Judged by `mrtr.input-request-methods`.

### MRTR-007

**MUST** · binds the server

> If a client request contains a `requestState` field, servers MUST treat `requestState` as an attacker-controlled input.

[`basic/patterns/mrtr#server-requirements-basic-workflow`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr#server-requirements-basic-workflow)

**Excluded.** A disposition toward an input, not an act: a server that treats state as trusted and one that treats it as hostile send the same messages until the state is actually tampered with, and even then what differs is the server's internal decision. The consequences the clause draws from it — integrity protection and rejection — are MRTR-008, excluded for their own reasons.

### MRTR-008

**MUST** · binds the server

> If `requestState` influences authorization, resource access, or business logic, servers MUST protect its integrity (e.g. HMAC or AEAD) and MUST reject state that fails verification.

[`basic/patterns/mrtr#server-requirements-basic-workflow`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr#server-requirements-basic-workflow)

**Excluded.** Both halves are invisible on the wire. `requestState` is opaque by construction — the specification's own examples range over base64 JSON, encrypted JWTs and serialized binary — so no check can tell an HMAC-protected blob from an unprotected one. The antecedent is worse still: whether the state influences authorization is a fact about the server's code. Verified instead by the implementation's own tests, where the key is available.

### MRTR-009

**SHOULD** · binds the server

> To prevent replay, servers SHOULD include the following inside the integrity-protected `requestState` payload and verify each on receipt: the authenticated principal, rejecting state presented by a different principal. a short expiry (TTL), rejecting state presented after it lapses; an identifier for the originating request, e.g. the method name and a digest of its salient parameters, rejecting state presented on a request that does not match.

[`basic/patterns/mrtr#server-requirements-basic-workflow`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr#server-requirements-basic-workflow)

**Excluded.** Names three fields that live *inside* the integrity-protected payload, which is opaque and generally encrypted — the trace carries the blob, never its contents. Two of the three also bind time and identity: expiry is a duration, which checks may not consult (LIFE-015), and the authenticated principal is not in the message.

### MRTR-010

**MUST** · binds the server

> Servers for which a given `requestState` must be consumed at most once (e.g., one-time redemptions) MUST enforce that invariant server-side.

[`basic/patterns/mrtr#server-requirements-basic-workflow`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr#server-requirements-basic-workflow)

**Excluded.** The clause's own words put the obligation server-side, and its antecedent — that this server's states are single-use — is a property of the server's design that no message declares. A trace showing one state presented twice would still not distinguish a violated invariant from a server for which none was ever claimed.

### MRTR-011

**MUST** · binds the server

> Servers MUST include at least one of `inputRequests` or `requestState` in every `InputRequiredResult` response.

[`basic/patterns/mrtr#server-requirements-basic-workflow`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr#server-requirements-basic-workflow)

Judged by `mrtr.input-required-has-content`.

### MRTR-012

**MUST NOT** · binds the server

> Servers MUST NOT send an `inputRequests` that the client has not declared support for in its capabilities.

[`basic/patterns/mrtr#server-requirements-basic-workflow`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr#server-requirements-basic-workflow)

Judged by `meta.no-undeclared-capability-reliance`.

### MRTR-013

**MUST NOT** · binds the server

> For example, if a client does not declare support for `elicitation`, the server MUST NOT include any `elicitation/create` requests in the `inputRequests` field.

[`basic/patterns/mrtr#server-requirements-basic-workflow`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr#server-requirements-basic-workflow)

Judged by `meta.no-undeclared-capability-reliance`.

### MRTR-014

**MUST NOT** · binds the server

> Servers MUST NOT assume that clients will fulfill the `inputRequests` or retry the original request.

[`basic/patterns/mrtr#server-requirements-basic-workflow`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr#server-requirements-basic-workflow)

**Excluded.** Forbids an assumption. Its wire-visible consequence would be a server that breaks when a client declines to retry, and a conforming session never exhibits that: the client either retries, which tells us nothing about the assumption, or does not, and the trace simply ends.

### MRTR-015

**MUST** · binds the client

> If a client receives an `InputRequiredResult` that contains the `inputRequests` field, the client MUST construct the requested inputs before retrying the original request.

[`basic/patterns/mrtr#client-requirements-basic-workflow`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr#client-requirements-basic-workflow)

Judged by `mrtr.retry-carries-input-responses`.

### MRTR-016

**MUST** · binds the client

> If an `InputRequiredResult` contains the `requestState` field, the client MUST echo back the exact value of that field when retrying the original request.

[`basic/patterns/mrtr#client-requirements-basic-workflow`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr#client-requirements-basic-workflow)

Judged by `mrtr.request-state-echoed`.

### MRTR-017

**MUST NOT** · binds the client

> Clients MUST NOT inspect, parse, modify, or make any assumptions about the `requestState` contents.

[`basic/patterns/mrtr#client-requirements-basic-workflow`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr#client-requirements-basic-workflow)

Judged by `mrtr.request-state-echoed`.

### MRTR-018

**MUST NOT** · binds the client

> If the `InputRequiredResult` does not contain a `requestState` field, the client MUST NOT include one in the retry.

[`basic/patterns/mrtr#client-requirements-basic-workflow`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr#client-requirements-basic-workflow)

Judged by `mrtr.no-unsolicited-request-state`.

### MRTR-019

**MUST** · binds the client

> The JSON-RPC `id` MUST be different between the initial request and the retry, as they are independent requests.

[`basic/patterns/mrtr#client-requirements-basic-workflow`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr#client-requirements-basic-workflow)

Judged by `mrtr.retry-id-differs`.

### MRTR-020

**MUST NOT** · binds the client

> They MUST NOT be used for any other request that the client may be sending in parallel.

[`basic/patterns/mrtr#client-requirements-basic-workflow`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr#client-requirements-basic-workflow)

Judged by `mrtr.request-state-scoped-to-retry`.

### MRTR-021

**SHOULD** · binds the server

> Servers SHOULD validate that the data provided by the client is a valid `InputResponses` object and that the information inside can be correctly parsed.

[`basic/patterns/mrtr#error-handling`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr#error-handling)

**Excluded.** Binds an act of validation, whose outcome is the only thing that reaches the wire — and a server that validated and accepted is indistinguishable from one that never looked. The outcomes the specification does pin are separate clauses: MRTR-023 for what a rejection may ignore, MRTR-024 for what a shortfall must draw.

### MRTR-022

**SHOULD** · binds the server

> Protocol errors (malformed JSON, invalid schema, internal server errors) SHOULD return a JSON-RPC error response with an appropriate error code and message.

[`basic/patterns/mrtr#error-handling`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr#error-handling)

**Excluded.** The antecedent is not identifiable from a trace: nothing in an exchange says whether the server met a protocol error, so an error response and a completed result are equally consistent with the clause. "Appropriate" is also unbounded — the clause names no code — and the shape an error must have regardless is BASE-052's, which is checked.

### MRTR-023

**SHOULD** · binds the server

> If additional, unexpected parameters are provided in the `InputResponses` object, the server SHOULD ignore any information it does not recognize or need.

[`basic/patterns/mrtr#error-handling`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr#error-handling)

**Excluded.** Requires an absence of consequence: a server that ignored an unexpected field and one that never read it produce identical sessions. The only failing form would be a server that rejected the request *because* of the extra field, and no error response says that was the reason.

### MRTR-024

**SHOULD** · binds the server

> If the client fails to send all the information requested in a previous `InputRequests`, and the missing information is necessary for the server to process the request, the server SHOULD respond with a new `InputRequiredResult` requesting the missing information again, rather than returning an error.

[`basic/patterns/mrtr#error-handling`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr#error-handling)

Judged by `mrtr.missing-input-reasked`.

### MRTR-025

**MUST** · binds the server

> Servers MUST validate request state as described in the server requirements above.

[`basic/patterns/mrtr#security-considerations`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr#security-considerations)

**Excluded.** A pointer back to MRTR-007 and MRTR-008 rather than a new rule, and it inherits their reason: the state is an opaque blob, so no check can tell a validated one from an unvalidated one.

## SUBS

### SUBS-001

**MUST NOT** · binds the server

> The server MUST NOT send notification types the client has not explicitly requested.

[`basic/patterns/subscriptions#opening-a-stream`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/subscriptions#opening-a-stream)

Judged by `subscriptions.only-requested-notifications`.

### SUBS-002

**MUST NOT** · binds the server

> The server MUST send `notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged` as the first message carrying the subscription's ID in `meta` under `io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId`, and MUST NOT send any notification on the subscription before it.

[`basic/patterns/subscriptions#acknowledgment`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/subscriptions#acknowledgment)

Judged by `subscriptions.acknowledgment-first`.

### SUBS-003

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> The client SHOULD check the acknowledged filter against what it requested and handle any unsupported types gracefully.

[`basic/patterns/subscriptions#acknowledgment`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/subscriptions#acknowledgment)

**Excluded.** Comparing two things it already has and reacting well to the difference: both the comparison and "gracefully" are inside the client, and a client that never looked sends exactly the messages one that did would. The server's side of the same exchange — honouring only what was requested — is SUBS-001 and is checked.

### SUBS-004

**MUST** · binds the client

> On stdio, where all messages share a single channel, clients MUST use this field to correlate notifications with their originating subscription.

[`basic/patterns/subscriptions#receiving-notifications`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/subscriptions#receiving-notifications)

**Excluded.** The client's own demultiplexing, which produces no message — the same clause TRAN-122 states from the stdio page, with the same reason. The wire-visible half, that the server tags every notification with `io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId`, is BASE-039 and is checked.

### SUBS-005

**SHOULD** · binds the server

> The server tears it down (e.g., during shutdown) — it SHOULD send a successful `subscriptions/listen` response to signal a graceful end (see Graceful Closure), then close the stream.

[`basic/patterns/subscriptions#cancellation`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/subscriptions#cancellation)

Judged by `subscriptions.graceful-close-result-shape`.

### SUBS-006

**SHOULD** · binds the server

> When the server ends a subscription on its own initiative (for example, during shutdown), it SHOULD respond to the original `subscriptions/listen` request with a completion result before closing the stream.

[`basic/patterns/subscriptions#graceful-closure`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/subscriptions#graceful-closure)

Judged by `subscriptions.graceful-close-result-shape`.

### SUBS-007

**MUST** · binds the client

> On stdio, if the connection is terminated and then re-established, the client MUST re-send `subscriptions/listen` to re-establish its subscriptions — the server holds no subscription state across reconnections.

[`basic/patterns/subscriptions#graceful-closure`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/subscriptions#graceful-closure)

**Excluded.** The obligation begins after a re-established connection, which is a second session: the evidence would have to span two recordings, and nothing in either identifies the other as its predecessor. Same boundary as TRAN-127, which excludes the restart that precedes it.

## CANC

### CANC-001

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> A client SHOULD send a cancellation notification to indicate that a request it previously issued should be terminated.

[`basic/patterns/cancellation`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/cancellation)

**Excluded.** The antecedent is the client's wish to stop a request, which produces no message of its own: a session with no cancellation is indistinguishable from one where nothing was abandoned. The same boundary TRAN-123's check records for the stdio half of this rule. What a cancellation looks like once sent is CANC-005's.

### CANC-002

**MUST** · binds the server

> A server MUST send `notifications/cancelled` referencing a `subscriptions/listen` request ID when it tears down that subscription stream

[`basic/patterns/cancellation`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/cancellation)

**Excluded.** The antecedent — the server deciding to tear a subscription down — is internal, and a stream that simply stops is indistinguishable in a recording from one the client closed or the network lost, so a missing notification has no falsifier. The message itself, when sent, is accepted by the checks it would otherwise trip: `meta.subscription-id-present` (BASE-039) and `subscriptions.only-requested-notifications` (SUBS-001) both treat a `notifications/cancelled` whose `requestId` names a `subscriptions/listen` request as the stream's own ending. Sending it for anything else is CANC-003's and judged.

### CANC-003

**MUST NOT** · binds the server

> Servers MUST NOT send `notifications/cancelled` for any other purpose.

[`basic/patterns/cancellation`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/cancellation)

Judged by `cancellation.server-cancels-only-subscriptions`.

### CANC-004

**MUST** · binds the server

> The server MUST treat a client disconnect as cancellation of that request.

[`basic/patterns/cancellation#transport-specific-cancellation`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/cancellation#transport-specific-cancellation)

**Excluded.** The cancellation page's statement of TRAN-069, excluded for the same reason: how a server treats a closed stream is a decision, and the trace shows only that the transport ended. The observable consequence — anything sent for the request afterwards — is TRAN-070's, judged by `transport.no-messages-after-cancellation`.

### CANC-005

**MUST** · binds the client

> The client MUST send a `notifications/cancelled` notification referencing the request ID.

[`basic/patterns/cancellation#transport-specific-cancellation`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/cancellation#transport-specific-cancellation)

Judged by `transport.cancel-notification-references-request`.

### CANC-006

**SHOULD** · binds the client and server

> Implementations SHOULD establish timeouts for all sent requests, to prevent hung connections and resource exhaustion.

[`basic/patterns/cancellation#timeouts`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/cancellation#timeouts)

**Excluded.** A timeout is a duration configured inside the sender, and checks may not consult time — the limit LIFE-015 records. A trace shows a request answered or not, never the deadline the sender held it to.

### CANC-007

**SHOULD** · binds the client and server

> When the request has not received a success or error response within the timeout period, the sender SHOULD cancel the request and stop waiting for a response.

[`basic/patterns/cancellation#timeouts`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/cancellation#timeouts)

**Excluded.** The trigger is the sender's own timeout expiring, which no message records and which checks may not compute from timestamps (LIFE-015's limit). A cancellation that is sent is judged for its shape by CANC-005; whether a timeout prompted it is not on the wire.

### CANC-008

**SHOULD** · binds the client and server

> SDKs and other middleware SHOULD allow these timeouts to be configured on a per-request basis.

[`basic/patterns/cancellation#timeouts`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/cancellation#timeouts)

**Excluded.** Binds an SDK's programming interface — what its callers can configure — which has no protocol representation at all.

### CANC-009

**SHOULD** · binds the client and server

> However, implementations SHOULD always enforce a maximum timeout, regardless of progress notifications, to limit the impact of a misbehaving client or server.

[`basic/patterns/cancellation#timeouts`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/cancellation#timeouts)

**Excluded.** A maximum timeout is a duration the sender enforces internally; checks may not consult time (LIFE-015), and a request still open when the recording ends says nothing about the deadline it would have hit.

### CANC-010

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> Cancellation notifications MUST only reference requests that: Were previously issued by the client; Are believed to still be in-progress

[`basic/patterns/cancellation#behavior-requirements`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/cancellation#behavior-requirements)

**Excluded.** Neither condition has a sound falsifier. A recording may begin mid-session, so a `requestId` the trace never saw issued may still have been — the reason `transport.cancel-notification-references-request` judges only that a request is named. "Believed to still be in-progress" is the sender's belief, and the page's own Timing Considerations make a cancellation that crosses the response on the wire conforming. The server-sent case is narrowed further by CANC-011, which is judged.

### CANC-011

**MUST** · binds the server

> Server-sent cancellation notifications MUST reference a `subscriptions/listen` request, to terminate that subscription stream

[`basic/patterns/cancellation#behavior-requirements`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/cancellation#behavior-requirements)

Judged by `cancellation.server-cancels-only-subscriptions`.

### CANC-012

**SHOULD** · binds the server

> Servers receiving cancellation notifications SHOULD: Stop processing the cancelled request; Free associated resources; Not send a response for the cancelled request

[`basic/patterns/cancellation#behavior-requirements`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/cancellation#behavior-requirements)

**Excluded.** Stopping work and freeing resources are internal. The one wire-visible item, not answering a cancelled request, is a MUST NOT on both transport pages and judged there at that strength: TRAN-124 (`transport.no-messages-after-cancel-notification`, stdio) and TRAN-070 (`transport.no-messages-after-cancellation`, Streamable HTTP). Judging it again here would report every such answer twice, once as a warning.

### CANC-013

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> The client SHOULD ignore any response to the cancelled request that arrives afterward

[`basic/patterns/cancellation#behavior-requirements`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/cancellation#behavior-requirements)

**Excluded.** Ignoring a response is the absence of a reaction inside the client; nothing it does with a late response reaches the wire.

### CANC-014

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> Both parties MUST handle these race conditions gracefully:

[`basic/patterns/cancellation#timing-considerations`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/cancellation#timing-considerations)

**Excluded.** Graceful handling is internal; the race itself is what a recording shows, and the checks are built not to convict it — TRAN-124 reports a message after a cancellation only once the server has demonstrably read it, and the conforming `stdio-cancellation-race` trace pins that. A party that failed to handle the race would show it through some other clause's violation, judged there.

### CANC-015

**SHOULD** · binds the client and server

> Both parties SHOULD log cancellation reasons for debugging

[`basic/patterns/cancellation#implementation-notes`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/cancellation#implementation-notes)

**Excluded.** Logging is local diagnostics with no wire footprint.

### CANC-016

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> Application UIs SHOULD indicate when cancellation is requested

[`basic/patterns/cancellation#implementation-notes`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/cancellation#implementation-notes)

**Excluded.** User-interface presentation, out by strategy rule 2: nothing a UI shows reaches the protocol.

### CANC-017

**SHOULD** · binds the client and server

> Invalid cancellation notifications SHOULD be ignored: Unknown request IDs; Already completed requests; Malformed notifications

[`basic/patterns/cancellation#error-handling`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/cancellation#error-handling)

**Excluded.** Ignoring a notification is the absence of a reaction, which a trace cannot tell apart from the notification never mattering. The party that sent the invalid notification is judged instead, where it can be: CANC-005 for a cancellation naming no request, CANC-011 for a server cancelling anything but a subscription.

## PROG

### PROG-001

**MUST** · binds the client

> Progress tokens MUST be a string or integer value

[`basic/patterns/progress#progress-flow`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/progress#progress-flow)

Judged by `progress.token-type`.

### PROG-002

**MUST** · binds the client

> Progress tokens can be chosen by the client using any means, but MUST be unique across all active requests.

[`basic/patterns/progress#progress-flow`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/progress#progress-flow)

Judged by `progress.token-unique-in-flight`.

### PROG-003

**MUST** · binds the server

> The `progress` value MUST increase with each notification, even if the total is unknown.

[`basic/patterns/progress#progress-flow`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/progress#progress-flow)

Judged by `progress.value-increases`.

### PROG-004

**SHOULD** · binds the server

> The `message` field SHOULD provide relevant human readable progress information.

[`basic/patterns/progress#progress-flow`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/progress#progress-flow)

**Excluded.** Whether a message is relevant and human readable is a judgment about its meaning, not its shape; any string satisfies the schema, and no mechanical reading of one decides relevance.

### PROG-005

**MUST** · binds the server

> Progress notifications MUST only reference tokens that: Were provided in an active request; Are associated with an in-progress operation

[`basic/patterns/progress#behavior-requirements`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/progress#behavior-requirements)

Judged by `progress.no-progress-after-completion`.

### PROG-006

**SHOULD** · binds the client and server

> Clients and servers SHOULD track active progress tokens

[`basic/patterns/progress#implementation-notes`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/progress#implementation-notes)

**Excluded.** Tracking is bookkeeping inside each party. Its wire consequences are the MUST rows beside it, which are judged: a reused token (PROG-002) and progress for a finished request (PROG-005, PROG-008).

### PROG-007

**SHOULD** · binds the client and server

> Both parties SHOULD implement rate limiting to prevent flooding

[`basic/patterns/progress#implementation-notes`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/progress#implementation-notes)

**Excluded.** A rate is messages per unit of time, and checks may not consult time — the limit LIFE-015 records. No count of notifications alone separates a flood from a long operation reporting often.

### PROG-008

**MUST** · binds the server

> Progress notifications MUST stop after completion

[`basic/patterns/progress#implementation-notes`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/progress#implementation-notes)

Judged by `progress.no-progress-after-completion`.

## CACH

### CACH-001

**MUST** · binds the server

> Servers MUST include caching hints on results with `resultType: "complete"` returned by the following operations: `server/discover`; `tools/list`; `prompts/list`; `resources/list`; `resources/templates/list`; `resources/read`

[`server/utilities/caching#cacheable-results`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching#cacheable-results)

Judged by `caching.hints-on-cacheable-results`.

### CACH-002

**MUST NOT** · binds the client

> Clients MUST NOT serve a cached response for a request whose method or parameters differ from the request that produced it.

[`server/utilities/caching#cache-key`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching#cache-key)

**Excluded.** Binds which cached response a client serves itself, and a cache hit is precisely the case where nothing reaches the wire. Serving from a cache produces no message: the client either sends a request or does not, and a session shows the request it sent, never the cached response it served instead.

### CACH-003

**MUST NOT** · binds the client

> Results produced by retrying a request through the multi round-trip requests mechanism&mdash;that is, requests carrying `inputResponses` or `requestState`&mdash;MUST NOT be cached, as they depend on inputs that are not part of the cache key.

[`server/utilities/caching#cache-key`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching#cache-key)

**Excluded.** The prohibited act is caching, which happens inside the client and produces no message. Its server-side shadow is honoured by CACH-001's check rather than left implicit: a `complete` result answering a request that carried `inputResponses` or `requestState` is not required to carry caching hints, because the specification does not ask a server to advertise freshness for a result nobody may cache.

### CACH-004

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> If `ttlMs` is `0`, the response SHOULD be considered immediately stale.

[`server/utilities/caching#time-to-live-ttl-field`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching#time-to-live-ttl-field)

**Excluded.** Serving from a cache produces no message: the client either sends a request or does not, and a session shows the request it sent, never the cached response it served instead. The freshness rules are worse still — they are stated in terms of elapsed time, and checks may not consult time (LIFE-015).

### CACH-005

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> If `ttlMs` is positive, the client SHOULD consider the result fresh for that many milliseconds after receiving the response.

[`server/utilities/caching#time-to-live-ttl-field`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching#time-to-live-ttl-field)

**Excluded.** Serving from a cache produces no message: the client either sends a request or does not, and a session shows the request it sent, never the cached response it served instead. The freshness rules are worse still — they are stated in terms of elapsed time, and checks may not consult time (LIFE-015).

### CACH-006

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> If `ttlMs` is absent, clients SHOULD assume a default of `0` (immediately stale) and rely on their own caching heuristics or notifications.

[`server/utilities/caching#time-to-live-ttl-field`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching#time-to-live-ttl-field)

**Excluded.** Serving from a cache produces no message: the client either sends a request or does not, and a session shows the request it sent, never the cached response it served instead. The freshness rules are worse still — they are stated in terms of elapsed time, and checks may not consult time (LIFE-015).

### CACH-007

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> If `ttlMs` is negative, clients SHOULD ignore it and treat it as `0`.

[`server/utilities/caching#time-to-live-ttl-field`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching#time-to-live-ttl-field)

**Excluded.** What a client concludes from a negative `ttlMs` stays inside it. The value itself is judged on the other side of the exchange: CACH-008 forbids a server from sending one.

### CACH-008

**MUST** · binds the server

> Servers MUST provide a `ttlMs` value that is `>= 0`.

[`server/utilities/caching#time-to-live-ttl-field`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching#time-to-live-ttl-field)

Judged by `caching.ttl-non-negative`.

### CACH-009

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> Once the TTL expires, the response is stale and the client SHOULD re-fetch on next access.

[`server/utilities/caching#freshness-calculation`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching#freshness-calculation)

**Excluded.** Serving from a cache produces no message: the client either sends a request or does not, and a session shows the request it sent, never the cached response it served instead. The freshness rules are worse still — they are stated in terms of elapsed time, and checks may not consult time (LIFE-015).

### CACH-010

**SHOULD NOT** · binds the client

> Clients SHOULD NOT treat TTL as a polling interval that triggers automatic background refetches.

[`server/utilities/caching#freshness-calculation`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching#freshness-calculation)

**Excluded.** Forbids a *reason* for sending requests, not the requests themselves: a poll and a genuine need look identical on the wire. Distinguishing them would mean inferring intent from inter-request timing, which checks may not consult.

### CACH-011

**MUST** · binds the client

> Implementations that do choose to poll MUST apply jitter and backoff.

[`server/utilities/caching#freshness-calculation`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching#freshness-calculation)

**Excluded.** Both the antecedent (this client is polling) and the obligation (its intervals are jittered and backed off) are properties of a request *schedule*, measurable only in elapsed time — which checks may not consult (LIFE-015) — and only across a run far longer than one recorded session.

### CACH-019

**MUST NOT** · binds the client

> Caches MUST NOT be shared across authorization contexts (e.g. a different access token requires a different cache).

[`server/utilities/caching#cache-scope-field`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching#cache-scope-field)

**Excluded.** A cache, and which authorization context may read from it, live inside the client or an intermediary: a hit serves a stored result without sending anything, so a cache shared across contexts produces no message. Nor does a trace carry the authorization context to compare: `mcp-trace-capture` records an allowlist of headers that never includes credentials, so no access token reaches the recording. Same boundary as CACH-002 (what a client may serve from its cache).

### CACH-012

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> When a cached page expires, the client SHOULD re-fetch that page using its cursor.

[`server/utilities/caching#interaction-with-pagination`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching#interaction-with-pagination)

**Excluded.** Serving from a cache produces no message: the client either sends a request or does not, and a session shows the request it sent, never the cached response it served instead. The freshness rules are worse still — they are stated in terms of elapsed time, and checks may not consult time (LIFE-015).

### CACH-013

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> Clients that require a consistent snapshot of the full list SHOULD re-fetch from the beginning (without a cursor).

[`server/utilities/caching#interaction-with-pagination`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching#interaction-with-pagination)

**Excluded.** The antecedent is a client requirement — that this client needs a consistent snapshot — which nothing on the wire declares. A client that paginates from a cursor is equally consistent with not needing one.

### CACH-014

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> If a cursor becomes invalid (e.g., the server returns an error for a previously valid cursor), the client SHOULD discard all cached pages and re-fetch from the beginning.

[`server/utilities/caching#interaction-with-pagination`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching#interaction-with-pagination)

**Excluded.** Discarding a cache is invisible, and the visible half — re-fetching from the beginning — is indistinguishable from an ordinary new list request. Serving from a cache produces no message: the client either sends a request or does not, and a session shows the request it sent, never the cached response it served instead.

### CACH-015

**MUST** · binds the server

> Servers MUST apply the same `cacheScope` to all response pages for a given list request.

[`server/utilities/caching#interaction-with-pagination`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching#interaction-with-pagination)

Judged by `caching.page-scope-consistent`.

### CACH-016

**MUST** · binds the server

> For example, if the first page of a `tools/list` response has `cacheScope: "private"`, all subsequent pages for that request MUST also be `"private"`.

[`server/utilities/caching#interaction-with-pagination`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching#interaction-with-pagination)

Judged by `caching.page-scope-consistent`.

### CACH-017

**MUST** · binds the server

> Servers MUST be aware that responses with a `"public"` `cacheScope` may be shared between callers even if the Result is coming from an authenticated endpoint.

[`server/utilities/caching#security-considerations`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching#security-considerations)

**Excluded.** Requires awareness. A server that has understood the sharing consequence and one that has not send the same bytes; what the clause is really asking for is the judgement CACH-018 then makes concrete, and that is excluded for its own reason.

### CACH-018

**MUST NOT** · binds the server

> MUST apply appropriate per-primitive access controls, and MUST NOT rely on `cacheScope` alone to prevent unauthorized access to primitives.

[`server/utilities/caching#security-considerations`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching#security-considerations)

**Excluded.** Access control happens before a response is composed, inside the server: a trace shows what one caller was given, never what a different caller would have been refused. Whether `cacheScope` was *relied upon* for that decision is a fact about the server's code.

## COMP

### COMP-006

**MUST** · binds the client

> Every request MUST include the required `meta` fields; see `meta`.

[`server/utilities/completion`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/completion)

Judged by `meta.required-request-fields`.

### COMP-007

**MUST** · binds the server

> Servers that support completions MUST declare the `completions` capability:

[`server/utilities/completion#capabilities`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/completion#capabilities)

Judged by `capabilities.completions-declared`.

### COMP-008

**SHOULD** · binds the server

> Servers SHOULD return standard JSON-RPC errors for common failure cases: Method not found: `-32601` (Capability not supported); Invalid prompt name: `-32602` (Invalid params); Missing required arguments: `-32602` (Invalid params); Internal errors: `-32603` (Internal error)

[`server/utilities/completion#error-handling`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/completion#error-handling)

**Excluded.** Each row's antecedent is a server-side determination — that this prompt name is invalid, that a required argument is missing — and a trace shows the answer without the reason for it. An exchange ending in `-32602` and one ending in a result are equally consistent with the clause, because nothing on the wire says which case the server was in.

### COMP-009

**SHOULD** · binds the server

> Servers SHOULD: Return suggestions sorted by relevance; Implement fuzzy matching where appropriate; Rate limit completion requests; Validate all inputs

[`server/utilities/completion#implementation-considerations`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/completion#implementation-considerations)

**Excluded.** Four quality properties, none of them a message shape: relevance ordering has no wire-observable definition, fuzzy matching is an algorithm choice, rate limiting is measured in elapsed time (LIFE-015), and validation that accepts leaves no trace.

### COMP-010

**SHOULD** · binds the client

> Clients SHOULD: Debounce rapid completion requests; Cache completion results where appropriate; Handle missing or partial results gracefully

[`server/utilities/completion#implementation-considerations`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/completion#implementation-considerations)

**Excluded.** Debouncing and caching are timing and cache-hit properties, both invisible for the reasons CACH-010 and CACH-002 record; "gracefully" describes what the client does after the response arrives, which is not a message.

### COMP-011

**MUST** · binds the client and server

> Implementations MUST: Validate all completion inputs; Implement appropriate rate limiting; Control access to sensitive suggestions; Prevent completion-based information disclosure

[`server/utilities/completion#security`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/completion#security)

**Excluded.** Security properties of an implementation, not of an exchange. A trace shows one completion answered for one caller; whether a different caller would have been refused, and whether the suggestions disclosed something they should not, are facts about the server's data and policy rather than about the message.

## PAGE

### PAGE-006

**MUST** · binds the client

> Every request MUST include the required `meta` fields; see `meta`.

[`server/utilities/pagination`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/pagination)

Judged by `meta.required-request-fields`.

### PAGE-007

**MUST NOT** · binds the client

> The cursor is an opaque string token, representing a position in the result set; Page size is determined by the server, and clients MUST NOT assume a fixed page size
